decisions.title: Systemic and Mucosal Antibody Responses Against Neisseria gonorrhoeae (Ng) Outer Membrane Vesicle Antigens following Four-Component Meningococcal Serogroup B (4CMenB) Immunization in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Phase II Trial
decisions.reason: This is a randomized human immunization and antibody-response trial, outside preparative organic-synthesis methodology.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The complete compact title explicitly identifies healthy adult immunization, systemic and mucosal antibody responses, and a randomized phase II trial. The compact abstract is empty, and the attempted Nature article could not be read. The exclusion relies on this unambiguous clinical-study identity, not an invented abstract or experimental chemistry.
decisions.challengeReason: Antigens and vaccine components are chemical entities, but the stated study objective is human immune response rather than a substrate-to-product preparation or a synthetic route. No borderline synthetic-method claim is being dismissed by a keyword filter.
decisions.evidenceSource: complete compact bibliographic title; publisher article access unavailable

decisions.title: The biogeography of giant viruses and interactions with Eukaryotes across European lakes
decisions.reason: Lake-virus genomics, host interactions and aquatic ecology are the principal contribution, not organic preparation.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The actual compact abstract describes recovery of viral genomes from European lakes, virus-host linkages, latitudinal abundance, light and resource effects, and associations with primary production. Its mention of aromatic organic matter concerns the lake environment, not a preparative reaction.
decisions.challengeReason: The second pass checked whether genomic methods or organic-matter terminology hid a synthesis contribution. The reported outputs are ecological distributions and host relationships; no organic reaction platform or completed synthetic route is identified.
decisions.evidenceSource: publisher-deposited title and abstract preserved in the pinned compact

decisions.title: The elongation of Mest transcript into MestXL sustains, but does not initiate, the maternal allele bias of its convergent gene Copg2 during neurogenesis
decisions.reason: The paper explains stage-dependent imprinted-gene dosage regulation during neural differentiation, not preparative biocatalysis.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The compact abstract reports a brain-organoid model, multi-omics, chromatin mapping and functional assays. Its two-step account concerns activation of the maternal Copg2 allele and subsequent MestXL-dependent repression of the paternal allele, rather than preparation of organic products.
decisions.challengeReason: The use of engineered cellular models does not itself constitute organic biosynthetic methodology. Unlike an enzyme-catalyzed transformation embedded in a chemical route, the article's stated outcome is a gene-regulatory mechanism, so exclusion is confirmed.
decisions.evidenceSource: publisher-deposited title and abstract preserved in the pinned compact

decisions.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Site-Selective C–H Arylation of Arenes: Using Diaryl Disulfides as an Arylation Reagent
decisions.titleZh: 钯催化芳烃位点选择性 C–H 芳基化：以二芳基二硫化物为芳基化试剂
decisions.reason: Arenes undergo preparative site-selective arylation using diaryl disulfides as masked aryl donors, with the method addressing both electron-rich and electron-deficient arene classes.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The actual compact abstract identifies readily available diaryl disulfides as a new masked arylating reagent and explicitly states applicability to electron-rich and electron-deficient arenes, including the difficult meta functionalization problem for electron-deficient substrates. The reported electrophilic-substitution interpretation explains site selection; it is not the sole contribution. No substrate count, isolated-yield range or scale is asserted here.
decisions.challengeReason: The specific alternative interpretation was a mechanism-only discussion of site selectivity. It is rejected because the abstract presents an aryl-donor strategy that changes preparative access across both electronic classes of arene. This is not a materials-performance study and is not supported merely by its C–H keyword.

scopeAssessment.primaryContribution: A diaryl-disulfide aryl-donor strategy for palladium-catalyzed site-selective arylation of arenes.
scopeAssessment.preparativeTransformation: Arene C–H positions are converted to aryl-substituted arenes using diaryl disulfides as masked arylating reagents.
scopeAssessment.generalityEvidence: The deposited abstract explicitly identifies electron-rich and electron-deficient arenes and discusses predictable site selection in multisubstituted arenes. Numerical scope, isolated yields and scale are not supplied by the obtained evidence and are not claimed.
scopeAssessment.boundaryChallenge: SEAr mechanistic language was tested against the actual method claim: the new arylating-reagent approach and applicability to contrasting arene classes establish a preparative contribution independently of the mechanistic explanation.

decisions.title: Visible Light-Mediated Dearomative Remote Functionalization of Arenes via a Tandem Strain-Release Spirocyclization Relay
decisions.titleZh: 串联应变释放螺环化接力实现可见光介导的芳烃去芳构化远程官能团化
decisions.reason: The central advance is a small-molecule preparative strain-release/dearomative spirocyclization relay, not biological evaluation of a fixed scaffold.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The actual deposited abstract describes a photocatalyst-free visible-light reaction platform combining bicyclo[1.1.0]butane strain release with remote dearomative functionalization of arenes. It identifies nitrosamine reagents and installation of sulfonamide and oxime functionalities into three-dimensional spirocyclic structures. These are article-specific transformations; no unobserved substrate number, yield, scheme or scale-up is claimed.
decisions.challengeReason: The reference to medicinally relevant functionalities could be mistaken for a medicinal-application paper. Here the reported contribution is the bond-forming relay and access to functionalized spirocycles, not imaging or pharmacological readouts. The abstract supports a transferable reaction mode with the named functional installations, so the preparative-method decision survives the challenge.

scopeAssessment.primaryContribution: Photocatalyst-free visible-light remote dearomative functionalization coupled to a strain-release spirocyclization relay.
scopeAssessment.preparativeTransformation: BCB-based strain-release addition/cyclization is combined with arene dearomatization and nitrosamine-mediated functional installation to furnish sulfonamide- and oxime-bearing spirocyclic products.
scopeAssessment.generalityEvidence: The obtained abstract specifies a reaction platform and the sulfonamide/oxime functionalization outputs rather than a single biological test compound. It does not provide numerical substrate scope, isolated yields or scale; those details remain unclaimed.
scopeAssessment.boundaryChallenge: Medicinal motivation does not replace the preparative assessment. The actual evidence is the BCB strain-release/dearomative relay and identified functionalized spirocyclic product access; no drug activity is being used as inclusion evidence.

decisions.title: Ammonia‐Gated Guanyl Hydrazone Photoisomerization Enables Sequential Solid‐State Optical Response in Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks
decisions.reason: The principal advance is gated solid-state photoswitching and sequence-dependent optical behavior of a hydrogen-bonded framework.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The obtained abstract names a tetrasulfonate tetraphenylethylene host and guanyl-hydrazone guest, cooperative framework assembly, acid-base-triggered crystalline/amorphous switching, fluorescence/color modulation and information encryption. These are specific photofunctional-material design and response measurements, not evidence of a general organic preparative method. The final abstract sentence is truncated in the compact and is not reconstructed.
decisions.challengeReason: Hydrazone isomerization and framework preparation are real chemical operations, so this is not excluded merely because it contains a framework. Their role in the stated work is control of solid-state optical output; the obtained evidence does not establish a general covalent synthetic or polymerization platform as its principal contribution.
decisions.evidenceSource: actual publisher-deposited abstract in compact, final sentence truncated

decisions.title: C 60 ‐Mediated d‐π Conjugation Induces Electronic Reconstruction to Boost Charge Storage of Nb 2 C/Nb 2 O 5 Heterostructure Anode
decisions.reason: Fullerene-mediated interfacial electronic engineering of a capacitor anode, rather than general organic synthesis, is the central contribution.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The actual abstract describes C60/Nb2C/Nb2O5 interfaces, charge transfer, electronic conductivity, lithium adsorption and anode/hybrid-capacitor charge-storage performance. C60 is an interfacial component; the reported platform produces and evaluates an electrode heterostructure rather than an organic product class. The final compact sentence is truncated and not invented.
decisions.challengeReason: The presence of an organic fullerene does not by itself establish an organic preparative method. The countercheck finds that the stated variations and measurements address interfacial orbitals and charge storage, not transferable carbon-bond construction or polymerization chemistry.
decisions.evidenceSource: actual publisher-deposited abstract in compact, final sentence truncated

decisions.title: Sandwich‐Like Supramolecular Clamp‐Templated Manganese(II) Bromide Scintillators for Multimodal Visualization
decisions.reason: Crown-ether/metal-bromide assembly is used to engineer scintillation and glass formation, not to establish general organic preparation.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The actual compact abstract reports four manganese bromides with benzo-15-crown-5/metal clamps, changing the associated cation to regulate tetrahedral geometry, X-ray charge collection, vitrification and light yield. The four prepared compounds are genuine materials examples; their number is not treated as organic substrate scope. The truncated final sentence remains unknown.
decisions.challengeReason: The challenge explicitly acknowledges preparation of four assemblies. Their comparison tests scintillator and glass behavior; it does not demonstrate a general organic reaction or a polymerization method. Exclusion follows the principal contribution, not a blanket prohibition on supramolecular chemistry.
decisions.evidenceSource: actual publisher-deposited abstract in compact, final sentence truncated

decisions.title: Ultrafast and High Charge Capability Aluminum‐Ion Storage With Long Term Stability
decisions.reason: The work develops a nickel-engineered Prussian-blue-analogue cathode for fast and durable aluminum-ion storage.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The actual deposited abstract centers on nickel-induced electronic self-compensation in NiCuHCF, suppression of lattice distortion, aluminum-ion diffusion, charge rate and cycling retention. Its production/scale language concerns an inorganic cathode material, not preparative organic or polymer synthesis. The final truncated clause is not extrapolated.
decisions.challengeReason: Large-scale material production is real preparation but not automatically an in-scope organic method. The article-specific countercheck ties that production to battery charging/stability and inorganic framework engineering; no general organic transformation is established by the obtained evidence.
decisions.evidenceSource: actual publisher-deposited abstract in compact, final sentence truncated

decisions.title: Electrocatalytic Carbon Dioxide Reduction Coupled with Alcohol Oxidation
decisions.reason: Paired electrolysis may represent genuine organic electrosynthesis, but the obtained evidence still does not resolve the preparative contribution.
decisions.evidenceBasis: The refreshed compact still contains no abstract for this DOI. A publisher search snippet mentions pairing cathodic CO2 valorization with high-value anodic organic oxidation, but the article/abstract/TOC fetches did not provide a readable full abstract, substrate-to-product scope or preparative evidence; the browser reader returned bot_blocked. The snippet is recorded as partial evidence, not a full abstract.
decisions.challengeReason: The title and energy-related index topics cannot justify exclusion, because a paired organic electrosynthetic method is plausible. Conversely, organic oxidation wording alone cannot prove a general preparative platform. Both passes therefore retain this specific DOI as pending; the missing evidence is not attributed to other reviewed candidates.
decisions.evidenceNeeded: Obtain the publisher abstract or relevant text/SI describing the alcohol substrates and oxidation products, the transferable preparative transformation, and scope or isolated-product/route evidence; distinguish this from an electrode/energy-performance-only study.
decisions.nextAction: Retry the article's textual abstract or supporting preparative sections in the next existing pre-review cycle; retain the original date and source review even after this DOI leaves the discovery window. Do not infer scope from keywords or retrieve TOC/body images for this review.

scopeRechecks.title: Isoindole-Based Multicomponent Synthesis of Pyrimido[6,1,2-cd]pyrrolizine Fluorophores with Unsymmetrical Urea Handles: Photophysical, Theoretical, and Antifungal Imaging Studies
scopeRechecks.evidenceBasis: The ACS Figshare landing page for supplement 10.1021/acs.joc.6c01559.s001 supplies the actual article abstract. It describes a one-pot multicomponent PP-fluorophore library with unsymmetrical urea handles, then side-chain-dependent emission, crystal packing, calculations and Candida imaging. This confirms real synthesis but does not by itself resolve whether the main reusable advance is preparation or probe-property diversification. The SI download redirected to an inaccessible signed PDF; no SI contents or figures were read.
scopeRechecks.challengeReason: Fluorescence and imaging do not automatically exclude a genuine multicomponent synthetic method. Equally, the word library and side-chain variation do not prove adequate general preparative scope. The actual reaction-partner variation and preparative section are still needed before affirming or overturning the old inclusion.
scopeRechecks.evidenceNeeded: Read the reaction design and substrate/partner scope plus preparative product evidence, sufficient to distinguish a transferable multicomponent synthesis from appendage tuning of an imaging scaffold.
scopeRechecks.nextAction: Obtain textual preparative evidence from the article or SI and repeat the primary-contribution challenge. Keep the existing card pending; do not delete it on the basis of access failure.

scopeRechecks.title: Protonation-Gated Strain-Release Generation of Amino-o-quinodimethanes
scopeRechecks.evidenceBasis: The ACS Figshare page for supplement 10.1021/acs.orglett.6c03499.s002 provides the actual abstract: protonation controls amino-BCB opening, with kinetic/barrier and half-life analysis, rapid [4+2] trapping and stable ammonium-precursor storage. These are genuine precursor/trapping operations, but the obtained text does not establish the preparative breadth of trapped products. The linked supporting file could not be read.
scopeRechecks.challengeReason: A storable precursor and on-demand generation strategy can have reusable synthetic value, so a mechanism-only exclusion would be premature. The counterpoint is that kinetics and gating dominate the obtained abstract; without the preparative trapping evidence, the old template-based include is not reconfirmed.
scopeRechecks.evidenceNeeded: Obtain substrate and trapping-partner variation, actual product preparation, and the article's preparative-method claim beyond barrier and lifetime measurements.
scopeRechecks.nextAction: Read the trapping/product-preparation sections and decide on general reagent/method value. Retain the existing card while this evidence remains incomplete.

scopeRechecks.title: Synthesis of a Fully Functionalized Chasmanine AF-Ring Fragment
scopeRechecks.evidenceBasis: The exact publisher title and the earlier scope-recheck queue identify a fully functionalized Chasmanine AF-ring fragment, not a completed synthesis of Chasmanine. A publisher search excerpt describes a stereoselective fragment route, but the complete article abstract/text was inaccessible. The route's independent general building-block value remains unverified; no full-text or original-date verification is claimed.
scopeRechecks.challengeReason: A fragment must not be labelled a completed total synthesis, but fragment preparation is not automatically out of scope when it supplies a general route or building block. The available title/search excerpt does not settle that separate preparative-value question, so neither deletion nor a new include is justified.
scopeRechecks.evidenceNeeded: Recover the authoritative first-online date without changing it, and read the actual abstract/route section to determine transferable building-block or methodological value and actual route completion.
scopeRechecks.nextAction: Recover the stored date and primary article text, then assess general fragment-route value separately from total-synthesis labeling. Do not delete the pending card or change its date.

scopeRechecks.title: Fine Tuning of Catalyst Active Sites to Access Advanced Ultrahigh-Melting Polyolefins
scopeRechecks.evidenceBasis: The preserved 2026-09-22 scope-correction review attributes an article-specific Wiley Early View statement to precontacting a pyridylamido Hf catalyst with allyltrimethylsilane, enabling polymerization of sterically demanding alpha-olefins. That is substantive synthesis counterevidence to a property-only exclusion. Current direct Wiley access was bot_blocked, so the actual monomer/preparation section was not reobtained under the new contract.
scopeRechecks.challengeReason: The first pass considered the preserved catalyst/monomer-access evidence sufficient to favor the old include. The challenge requires checking whether the claimed active-site method and monomer applicability, rather than ultrahigh melting behavior alone, are the article's demonstrated primary advance. The missing direct preparative evidence leaves this one existing-card disagreement explicitly assigned to pending.
scopeRechecks.evidenceNeeded: Read the publisher abstract and relevant catalyst/monomer-preparation evidence to resolve the relative contribution of polymerization method and material melting properties.
scopeRechecks.nextAction: Reobtain the primary article's textual catalyst and monomer evidence and resolve the recorded include-versus-pending challenge. Keep the existing card unchanged meanwhile.
